jobs.description:
Overview

We are seeking a Senior Scientist/Ecologist
to join our Henderson/ Las Vegas, NV
office.

Your role

Conduct/participate in natural resource field investigations, including but not limited to waters of the US; potential habitat for threatened and endangered species; vegetative community; presence/absence surveys, specimen collection and handling; construction monitoring; and stormwater and erosion control monitoring and compliance.
Prepares technical report of findings; supports preparation of permits and NEPA documents and provides peer reviews of reports prepared by others.
Is an Authorized Biologist for Mojave Desert Tortoise.
Serves and as in-field team leader for junior staff and technicians and\or coordinates with other Authorized Biologists.
Responsible for planning field work and coordinating with various parties as to when and where field work will occur.
Serves as an in-field team leader for health and safety requirements, including the preparation of safety documents and adherence to company safety protocols and procedures.
Maintains field notes and other collected data in an organized and useful fashion to meet and safeguard project objectives.
Effectively communicate the results of studies performed to project management staff.
Support proposal scope, technical approaches, and fee estimates.
Serves as an in-field point of contact for clients, subcontractors, and various other parties.
May assist in the management of projects.
Occasional work in afternoons/weekends as project monitoring requires. Not typically on a regular basis.
Performs such other duties as the Supervisor may from time to time deem necessary.

About You

B.S./B.A. or M.S. in a field of Natural Resources such as Wildlife Biology, Botany, Conservation Biology, Ecology. This level may be achieved by Scientists with minimum 8 to 10 years' experience since Bachelor's degree or 5 to 8 years' experience with Master's degree; typical incumbent has a minimum of 10 years' experience.
Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, technical writing, computer and communication skills desired.
The ideal candidate would have experience in identification of waters of the United States (including wetlands); Section 404/401 permitting including Nationwide Permits, related Pre-construction Notifications, Regional General Permits, and possibly Individual Permits.
Ability to obtain authorization from the USFWS
The ideal candidate will be familiar with regional flora and fauna.
Experience with Mojave Desert tortoise surveys as an Authorized Biologist is preferred.
Experience with BLM plant surveys and other rare plant surveys in California and Nevada preferred.
Impact analysis including NEPA and related documentation.
Stormwater and erosion compliance experience.
Wetland and stream condition assessment. Wetland and stream mitigation.
Basic stream hydrologic principles.
GIS skills and GPS equipment familiarity.
The successful applicant must have a general understanding of one or more of the following industries: infrastructure, transportation, state and local governments, or water quality.
Prior experience with the Las Angeles and Sacramento District of the USACE and NDOT projects preferred.
Experience with the Walla Walla and Portland/Seattle Districts of the USACE helpful.
Prior absence and presence survey experience as well as USFWS scientific permits or ability to obtain permits also preferred.
Routine travel is to be expected.
Must be confident working in harsh and inhospitable outdoor climates in the Western and Southwestern US during all times of the year.
Must maintain a keen awareness of safety protocols in the field and in the office.
Position may require use of company vehicle. Incumbent must have valid driver's license and a driving record that meets company policy.

Environmental Science Expert (AI Training)

About The Role

What if your expertise in climate modeling, ecology, or sustainability could directly shape how AI understands and reasons about the world's most urgent environmental challenges? We're looking for Environmental Science experts — Masters and PhD holders — to help build and train cutting-edge AI models by developing rigorous, real-world scientific problems that push the boundaries of machine reasoning.

This is a fully remote, flexible contract role designed for working scientists and researchers who want to apply their domain expertise in a new and impactful way. Full training support is provided — no prior AI experience needed.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Design, solve, and review advanced environmental science problems with real-world relevance and scientific rigor
Apply deep expertise in climate modeling, ecology, sustainability, or related disciplines to craft complex, nuanced problem statements
Collaborate asynchronously with AI researchers and fellow domain experts to strengthen AI model reasoning and accuracy
Evaluate AI-generated scientific content for accuracy, depth, and clarity
Ensure all deliverables meet high standards of scientific precision and communicative clarity
Work independently on task-based assignments at your own pace and schedule

Who You Are

Holds a Master's or PhD in Environmental Science or a closely related field
Deep expertise in one or more areas: climate modeling, ecology, sustainability, environmental policy, or earth systems science
Comfortable coding in Python or R for research, data analysis, or modeling
Exceptional written communicator — you can explain complex science clearly and precisely
Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and reliable when working independently
Fluent in English and based in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Australia, or New Zealand

Nice to Have

Prior experience with data annotation, evaluation systems, or AI training workflows
Background in scientific writing, peer review, or research publication
Experience working across interdisciplinary teams or in collaborative research environments
Familiarity with AI tools or large language model evaluation as an end user

Why Join Us

Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs and AI teams
Fully remote and flexible — work when and where it suits you
Freelance autonomy with the structure of meaningful, intellectually stimulating work
Apply your scientific expertise to a domain that matters — helping AI reason better about climate, ecology, and the environment
Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

The Environmental Specialist is responsible for maintaining compliance with federal, Louisiana, and facility requirements governing wastewater, stormwater, hazardous and nonhazardous waste, used oil, universal waste, and spill prevention. The specialist supports the site’s ethylene manufacturing operations, wastewater-treatment system, maintenance activities, laboratories, contractors, and capital projects.

Water and wastewater compliance

Review wastewater-treatment data, laboratory results and operating trends.
Identify results approaching permit limits and initiate corrective action before an exceedance occurs.

Nonhazardous and special-waste management
Manage nonhazardous industrial waste, wastewater-treatment sludge, contaminated soil, spent chemicals, debris, scrap materials and other plant wastes.
Compliance assurance and reporting
Conduct routine field inspections of wastewater, stormwater and waste-management activities.
Perform formal compliance audits against:
LPDES permit conditions
RCRA requirements
Louisiana hazardous- and solid-waste regulations
SWPPP requirements
SPCC requirements
Facility environmental procedures

Data management and recordkeeping
Maintain the environmental compliance calendar.
Maintain electronic and hard-copy records according to regulatory and corporate retention requirements.
Ensure data is entered into corporate systems agrees with source documents and agency reports.
Track at minimum:
Wastewater flow and analytical results
DMR calculations and submissions
Stormwater inspections and sampling
Waste generation and shipment quantities
Waste profiles and determinations
Manifests and disposal certificates
Inspection findings
Spill events
Training completion
Instrument calibration
Corrective-action status

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science or related field is Required.
Minimum of 3-10 years’ relevant environmental or sustainability experience in a petrochemical/refining facility and/or corporate office.

Specific Skills And Knowledge

Must have a level of proficiency with SAP, Internet, Email, and Microsoft Office programs.
Experience with State of Louisiana environmental requirements required.
Experience with RCRA regulations, SPCC, general knowledge of Clean Water Act.
Experience with TCEQ Regulatory Databases preferred.

jobs.title: Remediation Lead,
jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.

new_jobs.description:
This is where
your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your Role at Baxter

As the Remediation Lead, you will provide senior Quality leadership for the design, integration, and execution of complex remediation programs at Round Lake Drug Delivery. You will translate regulatory observations, inspection findings, quality-system gaps, and internal commitments into practical, risk-based plans that deliver sustainable compliance, protect product quality, and support patient safety.

You will serve as the single point of integration across remediation workstreams, establishing disciplined governance, clarifying accountability, managing interdependencies, and providing transparent, fact-based reporting to site and enterprise leadership. You will partner closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, and other functions while preserving the technical accountability of process owners and subject-matter experts.

This role is ideal for an experienced Quality leader who combines deep pharmaceutical compliance knowledge with strong program leadership, sound regulatory judgment, and a demonstrated ability to drive complex work to evidence-based and sustainable closure.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead the development, integration, and execution of site remediation strategies arising from regulatory inspections, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, health-authority commitments, audits, quality-system assessments, and significant recurring quality signals.
Translate commitments and identified gaps into clearly defined workstreams, accountable owners, milestones, dependencies, deliverables, interim controls, effectiveness measures, and objective closure evidence.
Establish and maintain a risk-based remediation master plan and governance cadence that provides clear visibility to progress, overdue actions, critical-path constraints, resource needs, decision requirements, and emerging risks.
Provide independent Quality oversight and constructive challenge to ensure remediation plans are technically sound, scientifically justified, regulatorily defensible, feasible, and aligned with commitments made to health authorities and internal governance bodies.
Drive cross-functional execution across Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Maintenance, Facilities, Laboratories, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, IT, Training, and Operational Excellence to remove barriers and maintain alignment.
Strengthen investigations, root-cause analysis, CAPA design, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, and effectiveness verification to prevent recurrence and improve Quality System performance.
Provide leadership and oversight for remediation involving sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, aseptic processing, terminal sterilization, sterility assurance, contamination control, particulate and microbiological risk management, process validation, and equipment qualification.
Coordinate the preparation and Quality review of regulatory responses, remediation status reports, inspection-readiness materials, leadership presentations, and supporting evidence packages.
Ensure remediation records are complete, traceable, internally consistent, inspection-ready, and readily retrievable, with a clear linkage between identified gaps, corrective actions, implementation evidence, and effectiveness outcomes.
Identify systemic themes, recurring failure modes, cross-workstream dependencies, and opportunities to simplify or standardize controls without weakening compliance requirements.
Partner with functional leaders to assess resource and capability needs, sequence priorities, manage scope and change, and escalate decisions that could affect regulatory commitments, product quality, patient safety, or remediation outcomes.
Create and monitor leading and lagging indicators such as milestone adherence, overdue-action aging, first-pass deliverable acceptance, CAPA effectiveness, recurrence, and evidence-readiness to verify that improvements are implemented and sustained.
Coach workstream leads and subject-matter experts on clear problem definition, measurable deliverables, disciplined execution, evidence-based closure, and concise executive and regulatory communication.
Serve as a trusted advisor to site and enterprise leadership, providing direct, objective assessments of progress, uncertainty, residual risk, and areas requiring intervention.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, Life Sciences, Quality, or a related technical discipline.
At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment, including significant experience in Quality, Compliance, or Regulatory functions.
Demonstrated leadership of complex, cross-functional remediation, compliance, Quality System, or transformation programs involving multiple workstreams and senior stakeholders.
Experience supporting FDA or other global health-authority inspections, regulatory responses, and remediation associated with regulatory observations, Warning Letters, OAI classifications, Consent Decrees, or comparable enforcement actions.
Strong knowledge of cGMPs, pharmaceutical Quality Systems, investigations, CAPA, change control, quality risk management, data integrity, validation, and inspection readiness.
Experience in sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing, including aseptic processing, sterility assurance, contamination control, injectable products, IV solutions, and/or terminal sterilization.
Ability to critically evaluate technical and procedural content, distinguish completed activity from demonstrated effectiveness, and identify weak assumptions, insufficient controls, or unsupported closure evidence.
Proven ability to influence without direct authority, make sound risk-based decisions, manage ambiguity, and drive accountability and follow-through across functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical information into clear, decision-oriented executive and regulatory updates.
Strong program and portfolio management discipline, including management of scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, resources, and change.
Ability to work effectively in a 24/7 regulated manufacturing environment and provide support outside standard business hours when significant quality, inspection, or remediation needs arise.
Ability to travel as needed to support regulatory inspections, remediation activities, and enterprise governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a scientific, engineering, quality, regulatory, or business discipline.
Formal certification in project or program management, Lean Six Sigma, quality management, or change management.
Experience leading remediation in a multi-building pharmaceutical operation or a complex sterile-manufacturing network.
Experience with electronic Quality Management Systems, remediation portfolio dashboards, evidence repositories, and executive governance forums.
Experience building organizational capability through coaching, leader standard work, structured problem solving, and disciplined performance management.
